bullets: Futures firm (S&P +0.2%, Nasdaq100 +0.4%) as CoreWeave's beat and raised guidance ease AI-slowdown fears after Monday's Nvidia-led selloff.
Hot October CPI lifted December Fed hike odds to ~88%; 10Y yield near 5% and a firm dollar remain the key macro headwind.
Asia mixed: Nikkei +0.85%, Kospi +1.2%, but Hang Seng -0.66%; Taiwan activated stabilization measures to stem AI-stock bleeding.
Energy (-6.7%) and Semis (-17.8%) are this week's worst sectors; PPI data due Thu Nov 13 is the next big risk event.

ILMN.why: Stock fell 18.6% on Nov 1 after Q3 revenue missed estimates despite raised full-year guidance. Citigroup cut to Sell (Nov 2) and Wall Street Zen cut to Hold (Nov 7), both company-specific calls, not sector-wide.
ILMN.bull: Guidance raised, margins and free cash flow healthy; sell-off may be a valuation overreaction.
ILMN.bear: Revenue miss plus two separate sell-side downgrades point to real growth concerns, not noise.

IFF.why: BofA cut IFF to Underperform from Buy on Nov 6, citing no near-term catalysts after the run-up and ~3% raw-material inflation squeezing H1'27 margins, despite a Q3 beat. A company-specific fundamental downgrade, not sector damage.
IFF.bull: Q3 beat, Taste & Scent strength intact, and three other firms still rate it Overweight/Buy post-earnings.
IFF.bear: A fresh sell-side downgrade flags real H1'27 margin risk from input-cost inflation, not just sentiment.

HPE.why: HPE fell with Dell and Super Micro in a broad AI-hardware selloff after the midterms reignited data-center spending/regulation worries; no HPE-specific miss, downgrade, or legal issue found (dd.moves is empty). Next earnings is Nov 23, just beyond the 7-day window.
HPE.bull: No company-specific bad news; still a Moderate Buy consensus; the sector panic looks overdone.
HPE.bear: AI-capex doubts are market-wide and durable; Nov 23 earnings could reset sentiment either way.
HPE.catalysts: Earnings call Nov 23 (slightly beyond 7 trading days); PPI data Nov 13.

VLO.why: VLO fell with the broader Energy sector (-6.7% on the week) amid Cramer-style warnings that refining margins are normalizing off decade highs. No formal sell-side downgrade found; Morgan Stanley held Equal-Weight and raised its PT (Nov 2), and the dividend was reaffirmed Nov 10.
VLO.bull: Dividend reaffirmed, margins still near decade highs, stock up 113% YTD; pullback looks sector-driven.
VLO.bear: If the refining-margin supercycle is ending as Cramer warns, forward earnings fall industry-wide, not just here.
VLO.catalysts: none found; PPI data Nov 13 could move the energy complex.

PR.why: PR's drop tracks the Energy/E&P sector-wide slide (-6.7%) as oil prices slumped. Wells Fargo trimmed its PT to $27 from $28 on Nov 6 but kept Overweight, not a downgrade. Q3 beat with record free cash flow and raised guidance; no company damage found.
PR.bull: Record free cash flow, raised guidance, Wells Fargo still Overweight; the sell-off tracks oil price, not fundamentals.
PR.bear: If crude keeps sliding, E&P earnings estimates get cut across the group regardless of PR's own execution.
PR.catalysts: none found; oil-price direction and PPI data (Nov 13) are the key macro drivers.
